html:
The Indian Premier League is a professional cricket league in India in which city teams play Twenty20 matches, short games of about three hours. It began in 2008 and is run by the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

It was the idea of the administrator Lalit Modi, after India won the first World Twenty20 in 2007. Teams were sold to companies and film stars, and players from around the world were bought at auction. The format of franchises, auctions and cheerleaders borrowed from American sport.

It became the richest cricket league in the world, with television rights among the most valuable in any sport. It moved the money and power of cricket further toward India, a shift that began with the 1983 World Cup win, and it made Twenty20 the format that drew new fans. Other countries started their own leagues on its model. The second season, in 2009, was played in South Africa because of the Indian general election.
